segments: A commuter in her thirties who carries a laptop, a water bottle and her lunch on the same shoulder every weekday, and wants the same bag to work for a Friday-night train out of town
A cabin-baggage-only flyer who has paid an airline surcharge at the gate once and will not do it again
A repeat CABAIA customer who already owns two or three pieces and is now buying the next one — often as a gift, often in a boutique rather than online

segments.name: A commuter in her thirties who carries a laptop, a water bottle and her lunch on the same shoulder every weekday, and wants the same bag to work for a Friday-night train out of town
segments.situation: Her bag has to survive a full office day and then double as the only piece of luggage for a weekend away, so she is choosing a format that oscillates between work and an overnight bag rather than owning two. Customers in this position report judging these bags on exactly that — the size that lets them switch between work and a 24h bag, the elasticated pocket running the length of the lining with pen slots, the padded laptop slot — and on whether the structure holds up when a laptop is in it. Some of them come away unconvinced on that last point: the sides and bottom not rigid enough, the laptop area 'too light to protect a PC', the fabric thinner than older models they owned. The decision is being made on perceived sturdiness, not on looks.

segments.situation: She is not evaluating the category; she is adding to a set she already trusts. Customers in this position say outright that this is their third purchase and they are still satisfied, that they own the backpack, the cabin case and now the 110L hold case, or that they bought three sizes of suitcase because they nest inside each other for storage. Several of them deliberately buy in a physical store, preferring contact with a salesperson to ordering on the site, and they notice that many — maybe all — of the colours are available in store. Gifting is part of the pattern: one buyer received hers as a Christmas present and called it magnificent. objections.objection: "A hundred euros for a fabric bag, two hundred for a soft suitcase — I can get something bigger for less at Décathlon."
objections.answer: Partly answerable. The durability case is on the page: accessories are 'conçus pour durer' and guaranteed for life, with wheels and trolley replaced free by customer service if they break; fabric handles tested to 110kg and straps and telescopic handle to 130kg; materials labelled GRS, EVE VEGAN and GOTS and external workshops certified BSCI or SMETA; free shipping from 50€ and free returns within 14 days lower the cost of being wrong. What is not answerable with current evidence is the comparison itself — there is no independent price-per-litre or durability comparison against a sports-retailer equivalent, and the one comparison on file is a dissatisfied customer's own.

objections.objection: "The new version feels cheaper than the one I already own — thinner fabric, no rigidity, a laptop slot that won't actually protect a laptop. The lifetime guarantee doesn't help if it just goes floppy."
objections.answer: Only partly answerable, and the gap should be admitted. Evidence supports the hardware and the structure claims — handles resistant to 110kg, straps and telescopic handle to 130kg, replaceable wheels and a lifetime guarantee that covers wheel and trolley breakage, padded laptop compartments on the Duffle and the Léonard handbag, snap buttons replacing Velcro and reinforced straps in the new Duffle. Nothing in the evidence addresses fabric weight versus earlier generations, base rigidity, or padding thickness on the Carry All, and the lifetime guarantee is published with no terms or exclusions at all. This objection cannot be beaten on fabric with what we currently know.

objections.objection: "The whole brand sells a lifetime guarantee, then the 99€ designer bag I actually want is only covered for two years."
objections.answer: Answerable, and honestly. CABAIA states plainly that CABAIA STUDIO collaborations are guaranteed two years, and explains why: these are limited-edition, small-series, ephemeral models on entirely new cuts and architectures, for which there will be no spare parts or long-term restock to support repairs beyond that period, while the same manufacturing and durability standards apply as to the rest of the range. The copy should name the two years rather than let the reader discover it.

objections.objection: "You list my airline as 'free in cabin', but your own page also lists Air France, KLM and British Airways as possibly charging extra — so which is it? I'm not risking a gate fee on your table."
objections.answer: Not resolvable from current evidence, and the material contradicts itself. The dimensions are solid (Carry All 37 x 27 x 16 cm; Duffle 29 x 30 x 45 cm) and the size table states clearly which lines are hand luggage and which must be checked. But one page lists Air France, KLM, British Airways, Iberia, American Airlines and Delta as carriers where the bag 'peut entraîner des frais supplémentaires', while other pages list several of the same carriers as 'inclus sans frais en cabine'; the Small soft suitcase is listed as free on Air France KLM, BA, Iberia, Indigo, Swiss and Lufthansa but with a supplement on Transavia and Easyjet; and the vendor itself warns that allowed dimensions vary by ticket type and tells the traveller to check before leaving. The same Carry All is also given two different weights on one page. The copy must not promise fee-free cabin carriage for a named airline.

objections.objection: "You advertise an integrated phone pocket and it doesn't fit a phone."
objections.answer: Weakly answerable, and the evidence is split against the claim. Documentation gives a specific limit — a dedicated pocket for a phone up to 165x80x25mm, and a bottle compartment taking containers up to 90mm diameter secured by an elastic — which is the honest way to state it. But customers contradict the unqualified feature line directly: one says that contrary to what the brand's AI assistant tells you, it cannot carry a phone; others say it is 'un peu juste pour tous les modèles', 'trop petite pour y ranger son mobile', while satisfied buyers say certain small smartphones do fit. The only defensible copy is the millimetre spec, never 'fits your phone'.

objections.objection: "It's out of stock online whenever I look, it takes nearly a week just to ship, and when I do order the parcel goes missing."
objections.answer: Half answerable. Orders ship within 4 to 5 business days of confirmation and standard or pickup-point delivery in metropolitan France takes 3 business days and is free from 50€; returns are free within 14 days and customer service is reachable Monday to Friday, 10h–17h30. Nothing in the evidence addresses stock availability, restocking, or lost parcels — and on the specific complaint that web-only promotions were refused on an in-store purchase, there is nothing at all. Do not promise fast delivery; the published shipping window plus delivery time is up to a working week.

objections.answer: Answerable without arguing. Buyers say exactly this and act on it — one bought in store because she prefers contact with a salesperson to ordering on the site, another notes that many (maybe all) colours are available in store, and a third had a defective bag exchanged quickly by the Annecy boutique. objections.objection: "Every brand says 'recycled' and 'vegan' now. Why should I believe yours?"
objections.answer: Answerable with named third-party standards rather than adjectives: materials labelled GRS, EVE VEGAN and GOTS, external production workshops certified BSCI or SMETA for ethical, social and environmental compliance, specific compositions (70% recycled cotton / 30% recycled polyester outer on the Carry All; 100% recycled polyester on the Duffle and the Porte-Gourde), and the lifetime guarantee as the durability half of the argument. Note the trap: elsewhere the same brand says only 'Ateliers certifiés' with no body or standard named, which is weaker than its own evidence — always name GRS, EVE VEGAN, GOTS, BSCI or SMETA instead.

objections.objection: "I already own a bag that does this. Why change?"
objections.answer: Answerable only on what the current bag cannot do. Three ways of carrying the same bag (hand, shoulder with integrated handles, crossbody) with an adjustable removable strap; a MOLLE system that lets the front and side pouches be swapped; a strap to attach it to a rolling case; a bottle pocket, a card pocket and a carabiner for keys; the Léonard sold with two straps, 65cm and adjustable up to 165cm. Plus free returns within 14 days so the comparison can be made at home. There is no evidence that a CABAIA bag outperforms a competitor's, so the argument has to be modularity and the lifetime guarantee, never superiority.

objections.objection: "Free delivery from 50€ sounds good until you're overseas — then it's 15 to 20 euros and eight working days."
objections.answer: Not answerable. DOM TOM delivery is stated as 15€–20€ with 8 business days and there is no threshold or waiver anywhere in the evidence. The only honest move is to state the terms and not imply that free shipping from 50€ applies everywhere — it is published for France métropolitaine.
